catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused on the cas_runner runtime engine, governance lifecycle actions, steering projections, and LLM abstraction layers.
analysis_limits: Repository source code inspected from pyproject.toml manifests, core runner modules, steering models, and governance pipelines.
Runtime execution traces and dynamic agent outputs were inferred from static architecture documentation and code definitions.

system_map.overview: cas_runner provides an automated continuous architecture and governance harness where agents operate through bounded pipelines (FlowRunner), evaluate compliance (ComplianceEngine), execute state transitions (GovernanceActionEngine), and steer architecture changes via structured prompt facts derived from git deltas.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Reconciles and merges incoming governance blocks, policies, and capability updates into repository state.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural and policy conformance against governance rules and produces structured findings.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step continuous architecture pipelines and coordinates step-wise context propagation.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner coordinates pipeline stages sequentially, invoking deterministic governance rule evaluation before dispatching LLM-driven synthesis and agentic reconciliation.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified gateway access across model providers with structured fallback handling.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Enables deterministic evaluation, testability, and guardrail validation in offline/CI environments.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Emits telemetry spans and traceable metrics for agent decision auditing and execution profiling.

state_and_memory.description: Capability records, lineage graphs, and governance decision logs stored as structured YAML/JSON metadata under version control.
Prompt facts and steering runtime indexes compiled from raw git diffs and current governance inventories.
Execution pipeline runtime context passed sequentially across steps in FlowRunner.

patterns.name: Declarative Steering Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Projects capability facts and git deltas into structured context indexes.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents hallucinations by feeding only verified, derived architectural facts to downstream agents.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Forces agent prompts to be constructed from structured git facts rather than unbounded repository crawling.

patterns.summary: Transforms raw VCS differences and capability definitions into verified, typed prompt facts to steer downstream agent generation.
patterns.intent: Ground agent reasoning in deterministic repository facts rather than unstructured prompt context.
patterns.context: Used during CI/CD architectural validation and projection builds where architectural delta must inform decisions.
forces: LLMs hallucinate or misinterpret file changes if provided raw unbounded git diffs.
Parsing code directly on every invocation introduces token overhead and nondeterminism.
patterns.solution: Aggregate GitChangeType and RawGitDelta into typed PromptFact instances compiled into a SteeringRuntimeIndex before prompting.
implementation_signals: Definition of PromptFact schema with categories and lineage references

evidence.note: Defines schemas for extracting structured prompt facts from raw VCS changes.

benefits: Auditable lineage between diffs and generated decisions
costs: Requires explicit projection logic for every newly supported file pattern
Schema changes require migration across capability definitions
failure_modes: Unmapped delta types may be omitted from prompt facts, blinding the agent to critical changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Extract the pattern of parsing VCS diffs into a strongly typed fact dictionary before passing them to prompt templates.

patterns.name: Finite State Governance Action Engine

tool_protocols.notes: Action engine validates allowed state transitions before persisting state.

optimisation_targets.notes: Eliminates illegal autonomous lifecycle transitions by verifying preconditions against a registry.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Restricts autonomous transitions to predefined, compliant state graph edges.

patterns.summary: Enforces permissible agent-driven governance actions through a centralized transition registry before actions mutate repository state.
patterns.intent: Prevent LLM or autonomous agents from executing invalid governance lifecycle changes or arbitrary status mutations.
patterns.context: Mediates state mutations for governance actions and capability promotions across lifecycle stages.
forces: Agents generating JSON actions can fabricate invalid status names or illegal transitions.
Manual validation per action type leads to scattered and fragile control flow.
patterns.solution: Route all requested GovernanceAction payloads through GovernanceActionEngine backed by TransitionRegistry to validate source and destination states.
implementation_signals: GovernanceAction model containing explicit action types and target states
GovernanceException raised on unauthorized transition attempts

evidence.note: Encapsulates transition validation against registered rules.
Provides data models and exception definitions for controlled governance transitions.

benefits: Prevents state corruptions caused by agent hallucinations
Centralizes audit and validation hooks in a single registry
costs: New lifecycle states require updating TransitionRegistry
Runtime exceptions must be caught and handled gracefully by caller
failure_modes: Missing edge in TransitionRegistry blocks legitimate autonomous resolution flows

patterns.reuse_notes: Use whenever an agent is granted write access to status flags or entity lifecycles.

patterns.name: Dual-Tier LLM Gateway Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Wraps LiteLLM and Mock client interfaces behind consistent contracts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Permits zero-token CI testing via MockLLMClient while retaining multi-provider support via LiteLLMClient.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standardizes call signature across real and simulated LLM operations.

patterns.summary: Decouples agent prompt invocation from specific providers through a LiteLLM adapter backed by a mock client for zero-cost testing.
patterns.intent: Enable transparent switching between real LLM providers and deterministic offline mocks without modifying agent logic.
patterns.context: Invoked whenever FlowRunner or AgenticMerger dispatches prompt tasks.
forces: Continuous CI workflows cannot rely on live LLM API keys or incur unpredictable latency and cost.
Hardcoded provider SDKs make model upgrades and vendor diversification costly.
patterns.solution: Implement a LiteLLMClient wrapper for production execution and a MockLLMClient adhering to the same interface for deterministic runs.
implementation_signals: Separate litellm_client.py and mock_client.py modules under cas_runner.llm
Identical invocation methods returning structured response objects

evidence.note: Production LLM client utilizing litellm router.
Deterministic test double for CI environments.

benefits: Zero token cost in automated CI test suites
Instant failover or configuration of alternative model endpoints in production
costs: Mock client responses must be maintained to reflect changing prompt formats
Subtle live provider differences (e.g. rate limits) are not caught by mock tests
failure_modes: Mock client drift where mock responses pass CI but live provider schemas reject output

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be applied to any Python agent application using LiteLLM for multi-provider isolation.

patterns.name: Rule-Grounded Compliance Evaluation

optimisation_targets.notes: Quantifies compliance objectively before triggering downstream generative tasks.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Applies deterministic rule validation rather than asking an LLM if a rule passed.

patterns.summary: Computes deterministic compliance findings and health scores on architectural assets prior to agent state promotion.
patterns.intent: Prevent downstream agents from acting on corrupted, non-compliant, or incomplete architectural configurations.
patterns.context: Evaluated during FlowRunner governance verification cycles and workspace bootstrapping.
forces: Relying on LLMs to self-evaluate compliance creates hallucinated approvals.
Unstructured validation errors make automated remediation difficult.
patterns.solution: Execute ComplianceEngine against CapabilityRecords and GovernanceInventory, emitting typed ComplianceFinding models and aggregated metrics.
implementation_signals: ComplianceEngine returning lists of ComplianceFinding instances
Metrics including compliance percentages, violation counts, and health status ratings

evidence.note: Implements validation rules and collects compliance metrics.
Defines schemas for audit findings and overall health evaluation.

benefits: Consistent, repeatable compliance scores unaffected by model variance
Actionable finding payloads that can be injected into agent prompt fixes
costs: Rules must be coded explicitly in Python or defined in strict configuration schemas
Static rules may lack contextual nuance compared to flexible reasoning
failure_modes: False positives block valid PR workflows when rules lag behind project conventions

patterns.reuse_notes: Couple deterministic rule engines with agentic loops as an upfront filter before allowing agent modification.

patterns.name: Agentic State Reconciliation Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Parses diffs and synthesizes merged governance blocks.

optimisation_targets.notes: Handles three-way merging of structural markdown and YAML blocks.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows agentic reasoning to merge conflicting non-trivial governance blocks where git merge fails.

patterns.summary: Applies targeted agentic reasoning to synthesize conflicting governance and architecture definitions into coherent unified blocks.
patterns.intent: Resolve semantically complex merge conflicts across markdown and structured YAML governance blocks that git three-way merge cannot resolve.
patterns.context: Triggered during project bootstrapping and governance synchronization workflows when merging global policies into local repos.
forces: Standard git merge conflicts fail when both upstream templates and downstream projects touch metadata headers.
Pure string-replacement risks corrupting custom local project adaptations.
patterns.solution: Use AgenticMerger to parse existing blocks, compare target upstream governance changes, and produce a ResolutionResult preserving local intent.
implementation_signals: ResolutionResult model containing success boolean and reconciled state payload

evidence.note: Reconciles incoming updates with local project configurations.
Orchestrates governance block merges during workspace initialization.
Contains output payload and status of reconciliation.

benefits: Reduces manual merge chore for distributed project teams
Maintains consistency with enterprise governance baselines
costs: Non-zero inference latency during workspace updates
Requires strict post-validation to verify valid YAML syntax
failure_modes: Agent accidentally drops custom local configurations during resolution if context window is saturated

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply when standard line-based merge tools fail to understand structural or semantic schema boundaries in config files.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline Context Propagation

tool_protocols.notes: Steps pass structured memory objects down the pipeline.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees evaluation and compliance verification happen prior to generation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Linear pipeline execution bounds agent unpredictability.

patterns.summary: Executes discrete architectural steps in a deterministic linear pipeline while propagating and enriching a shared execution context.
patterns.intent: Coordinate multi-stage architectural verification, steering compilation, and agent execution in an ordered sequence.
patterns.context: Serves as the primary entry point in FlowRunner for batch continuous architecture runs in CI/CD.
forces: Autonomous multi-agent loops can spin indefinitely or execute out-of-order without strict gating.
Downstream steps need access to artifacts produced by earlier validation stages.
patterns.solution: FlowRunner executes registered stages sequentially, verifying prerequisites before passing the mutable context object to the next step.
implementation_signals: Step results chained through context dictionary or typed container

evidence.note: Main pipeline runner executing stages in order.

benefits: Completely predictable step order with clear stopping points on error
costs: Cannot naturally branch into dynamic cycles without external loops
Latency is additive across all steps
failure_modes: An unhandled exception in an early stage halts the entire pipeline without running summary steps

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard pattern for CI/CD agentic harnesses where deterministic ordering must constrain model actions.

patterns.name: Telemetry-Grounded Traceability

tool_protocols.notes: OpenTelemetry spans instrument agent decisions and metric emissions.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables end-to-end auditability of decisions made across pipeline executions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Mandatory telemetry recording provides oversight without constraining agent generation style.

patterns.summary: Attaches traceable metric schemas and OpenTelemetry instrumentation to every governance decision and agent transition.
patterns.intent: Maintain a full audit trail linking source git revisions, agent model versions, and resulting compliance decisions.
patterns.context: Embedded across model evaluations and action execution within cas_runner.
forces: Black-box agent decisions create compliance liabilities in enterprise architecture.
Debugging failures in agent reasoning without timestamped metrics is error-prone.
patterns.solution: Define TraceableMetric models and integrate OpenTelemetry spans across the runner pipeline to record execution paths and outcomes.
implementation_signals: Presence of opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk in dependencies
TraceableMetric model capturing timestamps, status, and metadata attributes

evidence.note: Model representing telemetry and auditable metric entries.
Core runtime dependencies for telemetry collection.

benefits: Verifiable audit trail for compliance and risk reviews
Enables detection of latency spikes or prompt token inflation over time
costs: Requires export endpoint configuration in CI/CD
failure_modes: Metric emission failure may block pipeline if exception handling is missing

patterns.reuse_notes: Bind OpenTelemetry spans to every agent decision step and wrap results in typed metric objects.

patterns.name: Capability Lineage Anchoring

tool_protocols.notes: Lineage data models store ancestor IDs and origin hashes.

optimisation_targets.notes: Tracks which upstream capabilities and template versions an agent output is derived from.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can modify capabilities but must record origin IDs to maintain traceability.

patterns.summary: Tracks explicit provenance and evolution history across capability definitions using typed lineage records.
patterns.intent: Ensure that as agents propose or modify capability definitions, the derivation history and parent links remain uncorrupted.
patterns.context: Governs capability evolution across projects and the global cas-knowledge base.
forces: Repeated agent modifications erase initial authorship or source policy references.
Difficult to assess the blast radius of an upstream template change without parent links.
patterns.solution: Attach CapabilityLineage to each CapabilityRecord, recording parent IDs, derivation types, and evolution hashes.
implementation_signals: CapabilityLineage model with parent and evolution tracking fields
CapabilityRecord bundling metadata, content, and lineage together

evidence.note: Defines schemas for capability tracking and lineage.

benefits: Clear audit trail of capability evolution across system lifecycles
Allows automated pruning or deprecation of orphaned derived capabilities
costs: Agents must parse and preserve lineage metadata in generation steps
Increases prompt context size when lineage trees are included
failure_modes: Circular lineage references created if agent fabricates parent IDs

patterns.reuse_notes: Use structured lineage records whenever agents generate derived artifacts from source policies or architectural templates.

anti_patterns.name: Unconstrained Autonomous Merge
symptoms: AgenticMerger outputs are written directly to disk without verification by ComplianceEngine.
ResolutionResult status is assumed true without evaluating schema syntax or security constraints.

where_observed.note: Potential risk if resolution result is consumed without running post-merge compliance validation.

impact: Malformed YAML blocks committed to repository
Silent drift of mandatory enterprise security baselines in downstream projects
suggested_remediation: Require mandatory execution of ComplianceEngine.evaluate() as a pre-commit gate following any AgenticMerger operation.

anti_patterns.name: Raw VCS Diff Prompt Injection
symptoms: Passing raw unstructured git diff text directly to an LLM context instead of compiling it into PromptFact objects.
High token usage spikes when large binary or vendor dependency diffs occur.

where_observed.note: Architecture models explicitly mediate between raw diffs and typed prompt facts to prevent this anti-pattern.

impact: Context window exhaustion and high LLM API costs
Hallucinated diff analyses caused by unformatted git patch hunks
suggested_remediation: Always filter and transform RawGitDelta instances into discrete, categorised PromptFact items with strict file size cutoffs.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Defined via Pydantic models (PromptFact, CapabilityRecord) to enforce structured JSON inputs and outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Guarantees that generative prompts are fed strict facts and produce parseable governance commands.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrated OpenTelemetry SDK alongside dedicated TraceableMetric schemas for every step outcome.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Allows distributed tracing of multi-step pipeline actions and execution profiles.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Deterministic finite state validation through TransitionRegistry rejects unauthorized lifecycle actions.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Constrains LLM write autonomy so invalid promotions cannot occur.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent multi-project merge conflicts resolved when multiple agents update cas-knowledge concurrently?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If multiple CI pipelines run FlowRunner simultaneously against a central cas-knowledge repository, git lock contention or conflicting capability promotion may occur.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Repository shows single-workspace bootstrap and flow runner scripts, but distributed locking mechanism is not explicitly implemented in Python files.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine GitHub Action workflow concurrency configurations under .github/workflows/cas-continuous-architecture.yml.

open_questions.question: Does AgenticMerger support interactive human-in-the-loop escalation when confidence scores are below threshold?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Autonomous merge resolution without human review can lead to silent governance drift in production branches.
open_questions.evidence_gap: ResolutionResult contains success status, but explicit escalation hooks to GitHub PR review requests are not present in models.py.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Check governance action service implementations in src/cas_runner/governance/governance_action_service.py.
